intro: Tests correct use of either...or and neither...nor in everyday sentences

items.q: ___ my brother nor my sister likes spicy food.
items.why: Neither...nor links two negative subjects correctly.

items.q: You can pay ___ by card or by cash.
I don't like ___ tea nor coffee in the morning.
items.why: Neither...nor is the correct negative correlative pair.

items.q: Either you apologise ___ I am leaving this conversation.
items.why: Either...or pairs positive alternatives; 'or' completes the structure.

parts.title: Complete the sentences with the correct form.

items.pre: ___ the food nor the service was good at that restaurant.
items.why: Neither...nor negates both elements; starts the sentence.

items.post: next to me or next to the window — your choice.
my laptop is working properly today.
items.why: Nor is the second part of the neither...nor structure.

items.post: to the cinema or to the park this afternoon.

parts.title: Find and correct the mistake in each sentence.

items.sentence: Neither my colleague or I knew the answer to the question.
items.corrected: Neither my colleague nor I knew the answer to the question.
items.why: Neither must be paired with nor, not or.

items.sentence: Either she calls him, neither she sends an email.
items.corrected: Either she calls him, or she sends an email.
items.why: Either must be paired with or, not neither.

parts.title: Write your own sentences.
parts.pointsLabel: 2 points: 1 for correct form, 1 for meaning and use

items.prompt: Write one sentence about two activities you do not enjoy, using neither...nor.
items.criteria: Correct neither...nor structure; both activities clearly stated; verb agrees with nearer subject.
items.example: Neither watching reality TV nor playing video games interests me very much.

items.prompt: Write one sentence about two options you are happy to choose between, using either...or.
items.criteria: Correct either...or structure; two clear alternatives; natural everyday vocabulary.
items.example: I can either walk to work or take the bus — both options are fine with me.
